kamocore 0.1.1 - the KamoCore command line

Usage:
  kamocore <command> [options]

Commands:
  run               Run a suite or a project from this machine and report the result
  agent             Let KamoCore send requests into a private network through this machine
  runner            Claim the steps of runs you started and start your agent host on each, with the step's own credential
  deploy            Tell KamoCore a service or API was deployed, so it runs the affected suites
  mcp               Serve KamoCore to a coding agent as tools, over standard input and output
  scan              Read the services your files describe and the application in your code, and send them to a Designer code source
  check             Check a branch or pull request against its designs (kamocore check design), and fail the pipeline when asked
  check migrations  Check the database migrations a change adds for steps that lose data or stop a running release
  sql run           Run a SQL Tests project on KamoCore (kamocore sql run) and fail the pipeline when a case fails
  cache check       Run a Cache Tests connection's checks on KamoCore (kamocore cache check) and fail the pipeline when one does not hold
  ui run            Run UI tests in a browser on this machine (kamocore ui run) and fail the pipeline when one fails
  ui install        Download the browser kamocore ui run drives (kamocore ui install)
  whoami            Say which KamoCore the CLI talks to and what the token in the environment may do there
  login             Keep a token on this machine, for a person at their own keyboard
  logout            Forget the token kept on this machine
  completion        Print a script that completes kamocore's commands and options as you type, for your shell

Run kamocore <command> --help for a command's options.

Environment:
  KAMOCORE_TOKEN   The access token. It is read from the environment, or from the file kamocore login keeps; never from an option.
  KAMOCORE_SERVER  Where KamoCore is. Default: https://www.kamocore.com

result.stdout:
kamocore agent - Let KamoCore send requests into a private network through this machine

Usage:
  kamocore agent [options]

Options:
  --allow <host|host:port|*.suffix|range>  A host this agent may send to: localhost:5000, api.local, *.internal, 10.0.0.0/8 (required) (may repeat)
  --name <text>                            What to call this machine in KamoCore. Default: its own name
  --server <url>                           Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com
  --token-env <NAME>                       The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN
  --quiet                                  Print failures and the totals only
  --help                                   Show this help

Nothing is allowed until you name it with --allow, and the list lives on this machine: KamoCore is shown it, never
asked. The agent sends only to local and private addresses, and never to a link-local or cloud platform one.

The agent serves only the person its access token acts as, in the one workspace that token is for. It opens no
port: it asks KamoCore for work. Stop it with Ctrl+C; revoking the token stops it too. Give it a token of its
own with the scope ApiTesterAgent:write ("API Tester CLI agent") and no other: it opens nothing else.

Examples:
  kamocore agent --allow localhost:5000
  kamocore agent --allow 10.20.0.0/16 --allow *.internal

result.stdout:
kamocore runner - Claim the steps of runs you started and start your agent host on each, with the step's own credential

Usage:
  kamocore runner [options]

Options:
  --run <id>             Claim only the steps of this run. Default: any run you started
  --host <program>       The program to start for each step - your agent host (required)
  --host-arg <argument>  An argument for the host, in order; repeat it for each (may repeat)
  --once                 Stop after one step
  --beat <seconds>       Seconds between the heartbeats sent while a host works. Default: 300
  --server <url>         Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com
  --token-env <NAME>     The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN
  --quiet                Print failures and the totals only
  --help                 Show this help

Runs with your own access token (KAMOCORE_TOKEN, a kamo_pat_ token with Boards:write) - only the person who started a run may claim its
steps. For each step KamoCore opens it hands over the step's card credential, in this answer only; the runner starts --host with it in
KAMOCORE_TOKEN, the card's key in KAMOCORE_CARD and its branch in KAMOCORE_BRANCH, says it is alive while the host works, and claims the
next step when the host ends. Neither token is ever printed: both are taken out of everything the host and the runner write.

It stops when KamoCore refuses the token or the claim, after one step with --once, or when you stop it. A step's credential ends on its own.

Examples:
  kamocore runner --host claude --host-arg -p --host-arg "Build the KamoCore card you are assigned."
  kamocore runner --run 5d0c7f0e-... --host ./start-agent.sh --once

kamocore mcp - Serve KamoCore to a coding agent as tools, over standard input and output

Usage:
  kamocore mcp [options]

Options:
  --allow-writes                Offer the tools that change something in KamoCore. Default: read-only
  --allow-hosts <hosts>         With --suite or --project: offer running those from this machine, to these hosts only: localhost:5000, api.example.com, *.internal (may repeat)
  --suite <id>                  A suite the agent may run from this machine (may repeat)
  --project <id>                A project whose suites the agent may run from this machine (may repeat)
  --secret-host <name=hosts>    Give a secret to the agent's runs, for these hosts only: apiKey=localhost:5000, or auth:Staging login=api.example.com (may repeat)
  --secret-env <name=VARIABLE>  Read a secret from another environment variable: apiKey=MY_KEY, or auth:Staging login=MY_TOKEN (may repeat)
  --insecure                    Accept a certificate that cannot be verified
  --run-timeout <seconds>       Stop a suite run after this long. Default: 600, at most 3600
  --writes-per-hour <count>     With --allow-writes: how many changes an hour are taken. Default: 60, at most 600
  --server <url>                Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com
  --token-env <NAME>            The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN
  --quiet                       Print failures and the totals only
  --help                        Show this help

Speaks the Model Context Protocol over standard input and output: an agent host starts this command and talks to
it. Standard output carries the protocol and nothing else; what the server says to you goes to the error stream.
It answers hosts that open with a handshake and hosts that send their protocol version with every request.

Without --allow-writes the server only reads, and the tools that change something are not offered at all: running
a suite on KamoCore's servers, filing a bug, reporting a deploy, recording a r
[truncated]

result.stdout:
kamocore check - Check a branch or pull request against its designs (kamocore check design), and fail the pipeline when asked

Usage:
  kamocore check [options]

Options:
  --source <id>            The Designer code source the scans are sent to (required)
  --branch <name>          The branch to check. Default: KAMOCORE_BRANCH, the pipeline's variables, else what git says
  --pull-request <number>  The pull request to check. Default: KAMOCORE_PULL_REQUEST, else the pull request the pipeline builds
  --fail-on <results>      Fail the pipeline (exit 1) when any of these results is found: broken, missing, unplanned, different, unproven, rules (a break of a rule set to fail)
  --server <url>           Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com
  --token-env <NAME>       The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN
  --quiet                  Print failures and the totals only
  --help                   Show this help

KamoCore compares the latest reading "kamocore scan --source" sent for the branch or pull request with the designs the
code source is matched with. Each function of a design matches, is missing, is unplanned (in the code, not in the design),
differs, is broken (its linked tests fail) or is unproven (no evidence yet). The check fails the pipeline only for the
results --fail-on names, and never while KamoCore cannot check yet. On the Free plan KamoCore answers the counts only.
The access token needs the scope Designer:read.

Examples:
  kamocore check design --source 7c1d2e3f-... --pull-request 42
  kamocore check design --source 7c1d2e3f-... --branch feature/checkout --fail-on broken,missing
  kamocore check design --source 7c1d2e3f-... --pull-request 42 --fail-on rules

differs, is broken (its linked tests fail) or is unproven (no evidence yet). The check fails the pipeline only for the
results --fail-on names, and never while KamoCore cannot check yet. On the Free plan KamoCore answers the counts only.
The access token needs the scope Designer:read.

Examples:
  kamocore check design --source 7c1d2e3f-... --pull-request 42
  kamocore check design --source 7c1d2e3f-... --branch feature/checkout --fail-on broken,missing
  kamocore check design --source 7c1d2e3f-... --pull-request 42 --fail-on rules

kamocore check - Check the database migrations a change adds for steps that lose data or stop a running release

Usage:
  kamocore check migrations [options]

Options:
  --base <commit>                     The commit the change started from (default: the last commit's parent)
  --path <file|folder>                Check every migration under this file or folder instead of the change (may repeat)
  --fail-on <risky|destructive|none>  What fails the check: risky (the default, every flagged step), destructive, or none
  --junit <file>                      Write the result as JUnit XML to this file
  --project <id|name>                 Tell this project how the check went, so "Can we ship?" shows it. Counts only; needs a token
  --commit <sha>                      The commit that was built. Default: BUILD_SOURCEVERSION
  --server <url>                      Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com
  --token-env <NAME>                  The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN
  --quiet                             Print failures and the totals only
  --help                              Show this help

Reads the EF Core migrations (their Up method) and .sql files the change adds or edits - since --base, else since the last
commit, with what is not committed yet - or every one under --path. Destructive: a dropped table or column, an emptied table,
a DELETE without WHERE. Risky: a rename, a narrowed or changed type, a required column without a default, an index built
without CONCURRENTLY. A step a person accepts on purpose carries "kamocore: allow" in a comment on its line or the line above:
it is still listed, as accepted, and never fails the check. Only the text is read: nothing connects to a database, and no
access token is needed.

Examples:
  kamocore check migrations --base 4f2a91c --junit migration-check.xml
  kamocore check migrations --path src/backend/Core.Shop/Migrations --fail-on destructive
  kamocore check migrations --base 4f2a91c --projec
[truncated]

kamocore sql - Run a SQL Tests project on KamoCore (kamocore sql run) and fail the pipeline when a case fails

Usage:
  kamocore sql run [options]

Options:
  --project <id>       The SQL Tests project to run (required)
  --environment <id>   The environment to run against. Default: the project's default environment
  --group <name>       Run only the cases of this test group
  --case <id>          Run only this case (or separate ids with commas) (may repeat)
  --chained            Run the cases one at a time in their chain order, passing extracted values on
  --failing-only       Run only the cases whose latest run failed
  --junit <file>       Write the result as JUnit XML to this file, for the pipeline's test tab
  --timeout <seconds>  Stop waiting after this many seconds and ask KamoCore to stop the run (exit 2). Default: 1800
  --server <url>       Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com
  --token-env <NAME>   The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN
  --quiet              Print failures and the totals only
  --help               Show this help

KamoCore runs the cases on its own queue against the environment the project keeps, under the project's safety policy -
the same as Run all in the app. The CLI follows the run, prints each case that failed and exits 1 when one did; a case
that could not run (a plan limit, a stop) or a run that could not finish exits 2. No row and no value an assertion saw
is printed or written. The access token needs the scope SqlTester:write.

Examples:
  kamocore sql run --project 9a1b2c3d-... --junit sql-results.xml
  kamocore sql run --project 9a1b2c3d-... --environment 4e5f6a7b-... --group smoke --timeout 600

Usage:
  kamocore cache check [options]

Options:
  --connection <id>    The Cache Tests connection whose checks run (required)
  --check <id>         Run only this check, switched on or not (or separate ids with commas). Default: every switched-on check (may repeat)

  --quiet              Print failures and the totals only
  --help               Show this help

KamoCore runs the checks on its own queue, the same as Run all in the app. The CLI follows the run, prints each check that
did not hold and exits 1 when one did not; a run that was stopped part way or could not run exits 2. What a key holds is
never printed or written. The access token needs the scope CacheTester:write.

Examples:

kamocore ui - Run UI tests in a browser on this machine (kamocore ui run) and fail the pipeline when one fails

Usage:
  kamocore ui run [options]

Options:
  --site <name|id>               Run the site's ready tests; the site by name or id
  --test <name|id>               Run this test, by name or id (or separate ids with commas); a name is looked for in --site when one is given (may repeat)
  --tag <name>                   With --site: run only the ready tests with this tag
  --environment <id>             The environment to run against. Default: the schedule's, else the site's default environment
  --schedule <id>                Answer this schedule's turn: KamoCore counts the runs as the schedule's
  --parameter <name=value>       A plain parameter value for every test that declares it: name=value (may repeat)
  --secret-env <name=VARIABLE>   Read a secret from another environment variable: password=STAGING_PASSWORD (may repeat)
  --browser <name>               chromium, firefox or webkit. Default: chromium
  --headed                       Show the browser window instead of running headless
  --retry                        Run a failed test once more; the second run is the one reported, marked as retried
  --api-capture <connection-id>  Send the API calls of each test that passed to this API Tests browser sync connection, to review and make a suite of
  --allow-hosts <host:port>      With a card agent's credential: the host its locked tests run against, with its port: localhost:3000 (may repeat)
  --junit <file>                 Write the result as JUnit XML to this file, for the pipeline's test tab
  --timeout <seconds>            Stop after this many seconds: the running test is stopped and reported, the rest are not run (exit 2). Default: 1800
  --pipeline <name>              The pipeline's name, shown with the run. Default: BUILD_DEFINITIONNAME
  --pipeline-run <id>            The pipeline run or build number. Default: BUILD_BUILDNUMBER
  --commit <sha>                 The commit that was built. Default: B

kamocore ui - Download the browser kamocore ui run drives (kamocore ui install)

Usage:
  kamocore ui install [options]

Options:
  --browser <name>  chromium, firefox or webkit. Default: chromium
  --with-deps       Also install the system libraries the browser needs (Linux; needs root)
  --help            Show this help

kamocore ui run downloads its browser on first use; run this beforehand to keep the download out of a timed run or to
build it into a pipeline image. --with-deps also installs the system libraries the browser needs on Linux (needs root).

Examples:
  kamocore ui install
  kamocore ui install --browser firefox --with-deps

kamocore whoami - Say which KamoCore the CLI talks to and what the token in the environment may do there

Usage:
  kamocore whoami [options]

Options:
  --server <url>      Where KamoCore is. Default: KAMOCORE_SERVER, else https://www.kamocore.com
  --token-env <NAME>  The environment variable that holds the access token. Default: KAMOCORE_TOKEN
  --help              Show this help

Any access token may ask, and asking changes nothing. The token itself is never printed - only its kind, its name, its
workspace, its scopes and when it ends - so a pipeline can check its setup before it runs anything.

Examples:
  kamocore whoami
  kamocore whoami --server https://kamocore.example.com --token-env STAGING_KAMOCORE_TOKEN

kamocore completion - Print a script that completes kamocore's commands and options as you type, for your shell

Usage:
  kamocore completion [options]

Options:
  --shell <name>  The shell: bash, zsh, fish or powershell. (required)
  --help          Show this help

Load it once in your shell's profile. bash: eval "$(kamocore completion --shell bash)". zsh: the same with zsh.
fish: kamocore completion --shell fish | source. PowerShell: kamocore completion --shell powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression.

Examples:
  eval "$(kamocore completion --shell bash)"
  kamocore completion --shell fish | source
  kamocore completion --shell powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
